lead.headline: Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms opens India's biggest-ever IPO in a falling market
lead.hook: Jio Platforms is seeking ==up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) in India's biggest-ever IPO==, at a top valuation of 10.3tn rupees, as the Nifty 50 is down more than 12% this year.
points: Price range is 1,065 to 1,119 rupees a share for up to 270m new shares. Anchor investors closed on Monday: 212 funds, including BlackRock, Singapore's sovereign fund, ADIA and Fidelity.
Retail investors can bid from Wednesday. The IPO closes on Friday. Reliance is offering its 400,000-plus employees a discount of 54 rupees a share.

At the top of the range Jio would be India's fourth-largest company, behind Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank. That is more than twice the 4.9tn-rupee valuation set when Meta and Google invested in 2020.
The price is far below early hopes: a draft prospectus in the summer carried expectations above £110bn, so the valuation was cut sharply to fit a weak market.

Jio launched in September 2016, passed 100 million subscribers within 170 days and triggered a price war that made mobile data cheaper. It now plans to expand into AI, cloud and digital infrastructure.
signal: Global funds took the anchor book despite the downturn, which suggests the lower price was set to clear the market. If retail demand holds through Friday, it supports the view that the cut was the right trade-off.
lead.editors_read: Reliance chose a smaller raise at a lower valuation over delaying, which shows it values getting listed and the anchor demand above the headline number. If the issue is fully subscribed, it may reopen the window for other large Indian listings. A weak debut would show how far the market has repriced.

frontpage.headline: Anthropic's leaked S-1 shows a cloud capacity squeeze and huge losses
frontpage.hook: Anthropic lost $80.7 billion in the first half of the year on $16.3 billion revenue, and says it may spend more than $750 billion on cloud contracts, per a leaked S-1.
points: AWS, Google and Microsoft increasingly see Anthropic as a competitor rather than a customer, so it is struggling to secure enough cloud capacity, according to the leaked filing reported by the WSJ.
It is leasing its own data centers and using third-party operators, but worries they have a 'limited operating history' and may be less reliable than the big cloud providers.
Only two customers account for about a fifth of sales. The filing also warns that liability for harm caused by AI could exceed its insurance coverage.
Last week it told investors that third-quarter revenue alone reached $16.8 billion, up 45% on the previous quarter. It is reportedly targeting a November IPO.
signal: Its suppliers are also its rivals. If capacity stays tight, compute access, not demand, limits Anthropic's growth.
frontpage.editors_read: Anthropic's growth is real, but its dependence on rivals for compute is its weakest point. The IPO will test whether public investors accept a loss this size. Separately today, the KOSPI sell-off shows how sensitive markets are to AI financing doubts.

frontpage.headline: US bans DeepSeek AI tools across civilian government agencies
frontpage.hook: The US Department of Homeland Security ordered civilian agencies to stop using DeepSeek's AI tools, including third-party products built on them, and to remove them from IT systems.
points: The DHS cites data risk: DeepSeek's servers are in China, where the law gives the government 'extensive authority' to access company infrastructure. Agencies can request exceptions.

A December 2025 law had already restricted DeepSeek in intelligence national security systems. This extends the ban to civilian agencies, new purchases and existing systems. DHS cannot direct the military or intelligence services.

The US accused DeepSeek and five other Chinese AI firms, including Alibaba and Moonshot AI, of using distillation (training one model on another's outputs) to extract capabilities from US models, per a September report.
China's foreign ministry opposes 'overstretching' national security. Xi and Trump are due to meet at a summit in Shenzhen in November, where AI is expected to come up.
signal: Because the ban covers third-party tools built on DeepSeek, vendors selling to US agencies must check what models sit underneath their products.
frontpage.editors_read: The ban is cheap for Washington since few agencies likely depended on DeepSeek, but it sets a precedent for vendor supply-chain checks. Expect more pressure on open-weight Chinese models in procurement. The November summit may show whether either side trades AI limits for something else.

frontpage.headline: L&T Semiconductor and Tata Electronics to explore chip fabrication and packaging
frontpage.hook: L&T Semiconductor Technologies and Tata Electronics agreed to explore manufacturing L&T's chip designs at Tata's fabrication and packaging operations in India.
points: L&T is a fabless company (it designs chips but does not make them). Tata brings fabrication, packaging and testing.
They will assess manufacturing options for L&T's existing and future products, and design-to-fabrication optimisation for efficiency at scale.
Target markets are automotive, industrial, communications, security and intelligent-edge products, for Indian and global customers.
The companies also plan work on packaging technologies, manufacturing processes and quality systems. No investment figure or timeline was given.
signal: This is an agreement to explore, not a supply contract. If it turns into volume orders, it gives Tata's fab an Indian design customer.
frontpage.editors_read: Fabs need customers more than anything, and fabless firms need a local manufacturer. This pairing fits both needs but has no commitments yet. Watch for a named product and a volume figure.

frontpage.headline: South Korea's KOSPI falls 39% from its peak as AI stocks sell off
frontpage.hook: The KOSPI fell another 5% on Tuesday to 5,493.24, down 39% from its 9,386 peak, as doubts about AI spending, chip valuations and borrowing costs hit AI stocks.
points: SK Hynix is down about 35% from its peak and Samsung about 22%. Together they were 44% of the KOSPI in May, so the index moves with them.
The index fell 22% in July and a further 17% through October 16. It is still up about 30% in 2026 after a 116% gain at its June record close.

Triggers: hotter US inflation, which lowers rate-cut hopes, and fears over AI financing. Reuters reported OpenAI told investors September annualised revenue was nearly $50 billion, below the earlier near-$70 billion figure.
Last week's global rout wiped over $1 trillion from 20 AI and chip companies. Broadcom's CEO said capital could constrain AI more than chips or power.
Jefferies projects AI-stock earnings growth slowing from nearly 100% in 2026 to 30% in 2027, and urges diversifying beyond AI. The Fed meets on October 28.
signal: Markets with heavy chip exposure, such as South Korea, Taiwan and Japan, may stay volatile until AI financing and rate worries ease.
frontpage.editors_read: The sell-off is a repricing of how AI gets paid for, not of demand for chips. Rising rates raise the cost of the borrowing the buildout depends on. The Fed decision on October 28 is the next test.

frontpage.headline: Workers in southern India are training AI robots to replace blue-collar jobs
frontpage.hook: NPR reports that domestic and factory workers in southern India are being enlisted to train AI-powered robots, sometimes without their knowledge.
points: Tech companies plan AI-powered robots to replace blue-collar work, as AI is already expected to replace white-collar jobs.
NPR's correspondent found workers in southern India doing this training work. Some did not know their work would be used to train robots.
The source is a short podcast summary; it gives no numbers, company names or locations.
signal: If robot training relies on recordings of workers, consent and pay become the live issues. The summary gives no detail to say how widespread this is.
frontpage.editors_read: Robot-training data is the physical-world version of AI data labelling, and India's large labour pool makes it a natural place to collect it. Who is paid and who consented will decide how this plays out.

frontpage.headline: China adds export controls on tunnel boring machines that India's projects need
frontpage.hook: China will require export licences for tunnel boring machines, walking excavators and some dredger items from Nov 18, citing national security, which could hit Indian metro, rail and tunnel projects.
points: The controls are part of new restrictions on 14 technologies spanning AI, biotechnology and solar. Exporters must apply to China's commerce ministry under its dual-use export rules.
Indian projects at risk include underground metros, high-speed rail and tunnels, including in border areas.
In September 2025 Germany's ambassador said Chinese customs had blocked at least three Herrenknecht tunnel boring machines made in China for India. Later ones were released.
Herrenknecht responded by setting up production in India to reduce its dependence on China.
signal: Licensing gives Beijing a discretionary lever over Indian projects. If delays recur, buyers will favour machines made in India or elsewhere, as Herrenknecht is doing.
frontpage.editors_read: Licensing lets China slow shipments without banning them, which is hard to challenge. Indian project owners should check for tunnel boring machines on order from Chinese factories. Local production is the lasting fix but takes years.

frontpage.headline: India-New Zealand FTA takes effect with zero-duty access and 5,000 work visas
frontpage.hook: The India-New Zealand free trade agreement came into force on October 20, giving 100% of Indian export tariff lines duty-free access to New Zealand, where tariffs were up to 10%.
points: It is India's first FTA with full duty-free access across all tariff lines from day one. New Zealand also commits to facilitate $20 billion in investment into India over more than 15 years.
India gives concessions on 70% of its tariff lines, about 95% of bilateral trade value. Dairy, sugar and edible oils are excluded; apples, kiwifruit and manuka honey get quotas.

A new Temporary Employment Entry visa allows up to 5,000 holders at a time, for stays of up to three years, plus 1,000 working holiday visas a year. Post-study work rights run three years for STEM graduates.
Bilateral trade fell about 11% to $1.15 billion in 2025-26. The goal is to double goods and services trade to NZ$7 billion by 2030.
Moneycontrol finds India has negligible exports in 1,144 product categories where New Zealand imports about $6 billion.
signal: Gains depend on exporters actually using the access. The market is small, so the visa quota and the investment pledge may matter more than tariffs.
frontpage.editors_read: The deal's size is small, but the template is useful: full tariff access in return for protecting dairy and farm sectors. Services mobility is the part that may be copied in larger deals.

stories.headline: US sanctions Chinese venture firm over Google AI trade secrets case
stories.hook: The US State Department sanctioned Shanghai Zhisuan Technology, founded by Ding Linwei, a former Google engineer convicted this year of stealing Google AI trade secrets.
points: It also sanctioned Lu Qi's MiraclePlus, successor to a Chinese programme run by Y Combinator, and three affiliates, for providing seed financing to Zhisuan.
Measures may include freezing their US assets and banking restrictions.
signal: Sanctions now reach investors who fund startups accused of tech theft, not only the startups themselves.

stories.headline: OpenAI buys biotech AI startup Orchestra Bio
stories.hook: OpenAI acquired four-year-old Orchestra Bio, which reportedly raised about $20 million, to strengthen its life-sciences products; terms were not disclosed.
points: Orchestra builds AI agents that help biotech firms run drug discovery operations, from tracking finances to scheduling clinical trials.
The team and technology will join Rosalind, OpenAI's life-sciences model, and Rosalind Workbench, a tool to plan experiments and analyse results.
OpenAI says Moderna and Novo Nordisk are Rosalind customers.
signal: Startups worry the big labs will compete with them. Here the lab bought the startup instead.

stories.headline: Fireworks AI in talks to raise at $30-40 billion valuation
stories.hook: Fireworks AI is in early talks to raise at a $30 billion to $40 billion valuation, months after a $17.5 billion valuation in a $1.5 billion Series D in July.
points: It rents computing infrastructure and software to run, fine-tune and deploy open-weight and custom AI models. In July it said it passed $1 billion annualised revenue and 40 trillion tokens a day.
Rivals include Together AI, Baseten, Replicate, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Oracle.
Earlier this month an intruder used unauthorized internal credentials to access data from some customer accounts. Talks are early and targets could change.
signal: Investors are paying for the layer that runs models. The breach is a risk if customers question its security.

also.line: Otter.ai raised $320 million entirely from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund, which funds sales and marketing and takes a share of revenue it helps generate rather than equity.

stories.headline: OpenAI plans a humanoid robot demo in 2027
stories.hook: OpenAI expects to demonstrate an early humanoid robot prototype in 2027, but Sam Altman says humanoids in wide public use are several years away.
points: Altman says humanoids fit spaces built for people, so no building redesign is needed. Early focus is expected to be industrial: factories, facilities and data centres.
OpenAI lists 17 robotics roles, including motor, actuator and robotics safety engineers, suggesting it will build parts of the hardware itself.
It has not disclosed the robot's design, cost or manufacturing partners.
Tesla and Figure are rivals. OpenAI previously invested in or worked with Figure and 1X, so it could end up competing with them.
signal: The hard part is safe real-world intelligence, not the body. A 2027 demo says little about commercial timing.

stories.headline: China creates state-owned National Data Group in Xiongan to serve AI
stories.hook: China launched National Data Group Co in Xiongan, a state-owned company to develop and use data resources for AI, calling it a 'major strategic decision' by party leadership.
points: Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang attended the launch. Its remit is developing data resources, unlocking data value and fostering a data industry.
Xiongan has drawn 157 second- and third-tier subsidiaries of central state firms since 2023, plus China Satellite Network Group and China Huaneng headquarters.
Officials are reportedly courting AI, satellite internet and robotics firms that could reach 10 billion yuan valuations.
signal: The state is positioning itself as the main holder of AI training data. How it gives firms access will decide who benefits.

stories.headline: Alibaba's RISC-V designs have shipped in over 6 billion chips
stories.hook: Alibaba's research arm Damo Academy says over 6 billion chips have shipped using its XuanTie RISC-V architecture, as it targets AI and automotive.
points: RISC-V is an open instruction set free to use and modify, an alternative to Intel's x86 and Arm. It helps China reduce reliance on foreign chip design under US export limits.
Omdia forecasts RISC-V processor shipments growing nearly 30% a year, reaching about 25% of the global processor market by 2030.
The XuanTie C950, launched this year, delivers over three times the performance of its predecessor, the C920, Alibaba says.
The chief scientist says the biggest challenge is co-design: balancing computation, data movement and software for large models.
signal: The shipment count is large but likely dominated by small embedded chips. Running large AI models well is the harder test.

stories.headline: DRDO picks SSS Defence and Kalyani to build India's first aviation 20 mm gun
stories.hook: DRDO's ARDE shortlisted SSS Defence and Kalyani Group to develop an indigenous 20 mm aviation gun and turret for the Rudra and LCH helicopters; development should take about two years.
points: The two won the bid as Development cum Production Partners. After development, the order splits by cost: the lowest bidder gets 60% and the other 40%.
It is India's first design and development of an aviation medium-caliber gun.
The LCH's current 20 mm turret gun comes from European firm KNDS.
The turret gun is part of the armed helicopters' weapons suite for hitting ground targets.
signal: If trials succeed, the foreign-supplied gun on the LCH can be replaced by an Indian one.

stories.headline: IIT Madras alumni raise $9M to find new chip materials with AI agents
stories.hook: Discovered Materials, founded by IIT Madras alumni Akash Ramdas and Advaith Sridhar, raised a $9 million seed round led by Lightspeed to use AI agents to find new semiconductor materials.
points: Y Combinator and Peak XV also joined. The target is the heat from AI chips; the company says GPUs handle about 140 W/cm² and today's materials are at their limit.
Agents propose candidates, physics models trained by the founders simulate them, and promising ones are built and tested in labs. It runs Anthropic models in a custom harness, per TechCrunch.
Sridhar says Ramdas made about 20 guesses a day in his PhD; the agents now make thousands a day.
The company says getting a new material into a fab takes years and hundreds of millions of dollars.
signal: The pitch is a faster search, but the bottleneck the company names is fab adoption, which software does not fix.

also.line: A Rs 56.8 crore Bharat Dynamics tender to its former CMD's company is under scrutiny; five samples cleared technical inspection, financial evaluation is underway and no contract is signed.

stories.headline: FSSAI issues show-cause notices to Zepto and food brands
stories.hook: FSSAI sent show-cause notices to Zepto after a consumer complained of expired besan, plus to BMS Lifescience, HealthyHey Foods and Bakelite over misleading labels and claims.
points: Zepto must submit order logs, seller details, warehouse tracking, root-cause analysis and proof of stock withdrawal and refunds. The brands face licence suspension and penalties if they miss deadlines.
Its updated DRHP (IPO filing) discloses consumer, food safety, labour and Enforcement Directorate FEMA matters. Zepto paused its IPO until May 2027 after valuation differences with investors.
It is chasing a pre-IPO placement of about ₹1,000 crore.
FSSAI earlier pulled up BigBasket and Flipkart, and has penalised Amazon, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto.
signal: Platforms are being held responsible for what sellers list, which raises compliance cost for quick commerce ahead of IPOs.

stories.headline: Tenstorrent raises $1.5 billion, valuing it at $6.2 billion
stories.hook: AI chip startup Tenstorrent raised $1.5 billion in a Series E at a $6.2 billion post-money valuation, more than double its December 2024 level.
points: Trace Capital and Innovation X led. ARK Invest, Sandisk, Morgan Stanley, T Rowe Price and Tether also joined.
The money will scale production of Galaxy servers, which combine dozens of its chips for chatbots, coding assistants and video generation.
It uses RISC-V, an open architecture that needs no licence fees and reduces dependence on Arm.
CEO Jim Keller previously led Tesla's self-driving chip effort. The December 2024 round raised over $693 million at a $2 billion pre-money valuation.
signal: Money is flowing to non-Nvidia AI chips on open architectures. Production scale is the test.

stories.headline: India curtailed 96.9 GW of solar in September, 79% of curtailed energy from Gujarat and Rajasthan
stories.hook: India curtailed (switched off) 96.9 GW of solar in September, part of 118.6 GW of renewables, equal to 1.28% of total, per JMK; that is 24% below a year earlier.
points: From May to August 2026 curtailment was four times the level of 2025. JMK calls September's drop 'seasonal relief' rather than structural improvement.
Of September's curtailment, 61% was emergency TRAS Down orders (cuts to balance supply and demand) and 39% real-time system constraints, so it was mainly balancing, not congestion alone.
Gujarat and Rajasthan produced 79% of the curtailed energy.
Avoiding it in September would have needed 12.6 GWh a day of storage, equal to 3GW of 4-hour batteries.
India added about 44.6 GW of solar in FY2026. ICRA says transmission needs about 20,000 circuit km of lines a year; India is expected to spend ₹5 trillion ($52 billion) in 2027-2032.
signal: __Storage of about 3 GW (4-hour) in Gujarat and Rajasthan__ would absorb recurring surpluses, JMK says, alongside transmission upgrades.

stories.headline: India weighs agrivoltaics support, eyes 5 GW in 3-4 years
stories.hook: MNRE is considering a support scheme for agrivoltaics (solar panels raised above crops) and sees about 5 GW being added over three to four years.
points: The ministry says agrivoltaic projects cost 25-30% more than ground-mounted solar because panels must be elevated. The scheme would cover that gap.
Power cost is estimated at ₹3.20-3.30 per kWh against ₹2.80-3 for PM-KUSUM decentralised solar.
It is deciding whether to fit the scheme into PM-KUSUM or make a separate one, with the Finance Ministry. The 5 GW also depends on state feed-in tariffs.
Trials with IARI found fruits and leafy vegetables work, but rice and sugarcane do not do as well.
Five states hold 85% of solar deployment; agrivoltaics could spread it to land-scarce states.
signal: If states set viable tariffs, solar can expand without taking farmland. Without them the 5 GW target is at risk.

also.line: More than 50 companies including Reliance, Adani and L&T are vying for India's green hydrogen market; 15 firms were awarded 3 GW a year of electrolyser manufacturing capacity.

stories.headline: Rubio says India-US trade deal is 'incredibly close', weeks away
stories.hook: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the India-US trade deal is 'incredibly close' and expected in 'weeks, not months', with only technical details and a small number of items left.
points: Rubio said the two sides must agree the language means the same thing. He hopes for an announcement soon, then leaders signing.
He urged India to buy more US energy and technology, called India a refining 'superpower' and pushed processing Venezuelan crude. He visits Reliance's Jamnagar refinery on Wednesday.
Ties have been strained by US tariffs imposed last year, a higher H-1B fee and a restriction on a green-card processing programme for firms including TCS and Wipro.
Last week Trump suspended some sanctions on Russia and five of the biggest buyers of Russian oil, including India.
signal: If the final items are technical, a deal could land soon. The energy and defence purchases the US is pressing for could be the price.

stories.headline: WSJ: Musk ordered slowdown of Starlink service used by Ukraine's military
stories.hook: The WSJ reports that Elon Musk last week ordered a slowdown of a military-grade Starlink service Ukraine relies on, hurting its drone missions; Reuters could not verify.
points: Ukraine uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations. Zelensky said the cut came at 1 am and he is sure it was deliberate.

Hegseth and Rubio deny Washington ordered it; Rubio says Starlink speed has been restored. Musk said US military or the president set the limits. Reuters earlier reported the order came from the White House.
Ukraine seeks access to Starshield, the US military system, for deep strikes in Russia. Fedorov says Starlink is being restored and wants Starshield's speed limit removed.
Ties between Kyiv and Washington are at new lows after Trump's Russian diesel deal and sanctions waiver.
signal: A single private company's settings can shape a war, so who controls the throttle is a policy question.

also.line: Indian firms struggle to fill cybersecurity roles even as rogue AI agents raise risk; staffing data show a widening gap between demand and supply, with only a fraction of vacancies filled.
EU unveils new Arctic strategy with focus on security (source unreachable — headline only)

stories.headline: 12,700 Indian tech workers returned from the US by September
stories.hook: About 12,700 Indian tech professionals had left the US for India by September 2026, on track to pass last year's record of 15,100, per Xpheno data.
points: Returns rose from 7,200 in 2023 to 9,800 in 2024. Causes cited are visa uncertainty, layoffs and unstable hiring.

PERM (the labour-certification step for employer-sponsored green cards) processing is suspended for large recruiters including Microsoft, Infosys, Cognizant, Wipro and Tata. Existing H-1Bs and approved green cards are unaffected.
A bill introduced Oct. 1 would raise fines for H-1B violations to up to $250,000 and allow bans of up to 10 years.
Returning is not easy: Indian employers prefer AI, cloud, cybersecurity and product leadership skills over general overseas experience.
signal: Returnees with AI, cloud and product skills are likely to find the best offers in India.

also.line: Tata Consultancy Services completed its acquisition of Best Buy's India GCC (global capability centre), establishing an AI-native capability centre (source unreachable — headline only)
Drought-hit maize supply is squeezing poultry feed, ethanol and starch makers, who are competing for the grain; maize also ties into India's efforts to cut crude imports.

opportunities.name: AI and National Security Convergence Fellowship 2026-2027
opportunities.summary: Seven-month fellowship for 15 mid-career professionals on keeping AI under human control, with in-person sessions in Washington DC. Requires DC residence and US or allied citizenship, so likely not open to him.

opportunities.name: Primewise Founders Club Networking Event - Jaipur (Online)
opportunities.summary: Online session for 25-40 selected founders and investors, with 50-second spotlights and breakout rooms. Complete the confirmation form first, as Meetup registration alone does not secure a seat.

opportunities.name: Neural Storm 2026
opportunities.summary: 48-hour AI/ML hackathon with three tracks and 15 problem statements. Submit a working deployed demo and a public GitHub repo. Online.

opportunities.name: Homingo Hack Days: Online AI Hackathon
opportunities.summary: Free online hackathon in Agents, Automation or LLM apps, open to anyone in India, solo or teams of 2-4. Winner gets Rs 5,000. Register on the Homingo site, not only Unstop.
